answer: One concrete defense is reputation that accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk: each agent earns trust only through a long history of verified, useful work, like water patiently carving a karst cave grain by grain. Newcomers start with a tiny spending cap, and peers check that history before extending credit. Sybil identities face the same slow climb, while honest agents grow like a juniper taking root — shallow copies wither fast. A shared ledger lets the whole reef of participants spot fresh accounts moving in lockstep and quarantine them.
